summary:
nuget.org GET api/v2/verifykey/{id}/{version} first evaluates the user's PackageVerify security policies and returns HTTP 400 with the policy error message if they fail. The Default subscription lists RequirePackageVerifyScopePolicy, which succeeds only when the calling key carries the explicit package:verify scope. Per the cited source, otherwise the handler returns the error SecurityPolicy_RequireApiKeyWithPackageVerifyScope ("A package verification key is required to push symbols. Please contact support@nuget.org to get more details."). Trusted Publishing short-lived keys from NuGet/login@v1 carry push scopes, so the refusal is expected every time: by design, not a service defect. That policy applies when EnforceDefaultSecurityPolicies is on; the setting is inferred from observed nuget.org behaviour, not read from configuration.

Diagnosis: nuget.org's IIS replaces the 400 body with the 11-byte text Bad Request, while the HTTP reason phrase carries the real policy text. Diagnose from the reason phrase, not the body. nuget.org also labels plain-text errors text/html. This explains the earlier record github/nuget-trusted-publishing-policy-scope, where the all-400 authorization probes showed no known policy-text match because only bodies were retained; that record is cross-referenced, not superseded or contradicted.

Observed evidence: FS.GG.Rendering run 40987145442 attempt 1. All 19 FS.GG.UI* observations had body sha256 7c41b898c5da0cfa4aa049b65ef50248bce9a72d24bef4c723786431921b75aa (the bytes of Bad Request) and reason-phrase sha256 89512b21e84e24453eeece2d621e909c238ed9b15f077044a07d5804beaf869c (the exact 109-byte SecurityPolicy_RequireApiKeyWithPackageVerifyScope text). Both digests were independently recomputed from the cited resource string and the literal body.

Consequence and decision: a pre-push verifykey gate cannot prove Trusted Publishing push scope. A derived package-verification key (created from the original key) carries the verify scope only and so does not prove the original key's push scope either. FS-GG therefore treats verifykey as advisory and protects publication with a canary-first ordered push. That change is FS.GG.Rendering PR #1488, which was open and unmerged when this record was captured; this record does not establish that it landed.

Limits: whether the 2026-10-22 verification pass used a Trusted Publishing key is not established here. Policy enforcement configuration is inferred from behaviour. The cited Gallery source is revision c25bab04 and may differ from the deployed service. This record grants no publication, retry, gate waiver or policy change.
title: nuget.org verifykey refuses Trusted Publishing keys by policy; use it as advisory only
